items.pronunciation_notes: Three words all ending in a short e, with a nasal only on the last: ve jaa-te hoṁ-ge.

learn.title_en: A habit you are assuming rather than reporting
learn.explanation_en: वे जाते होंगे means they probably go, and it is a specific and useful thing to be able to say: you are describing someone's routine without claiming to have observed it. That is a distinction English usually handles by adding a word — probably, I suppose, they must — and Hindi handles inside the verb. Grammatically nothing here is new. The habitual participle is the one you built at level two, and होंगे is the plural presumptive from the last level.

examples.note: An assumed habit rather than an observed one.
The most natural use of this cell — guessing about where someone lives.
The feminine singular, with both words agreeing.

common_error.why_en: होगा is singular. The presumptive counts in the third person exactly as the past auxiliary does.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · वे · masculine plural · habitual presumptive
practice.question_read_as: jaanaa · ve · masculine plural · habitual presumptive
practice.explanation_en: Habitual participle जाते with the plural presumptive auxiliary होंगे.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: वे जा रहे होंगे — they are probably going right now.

items.pronunciation_notes: हूँगा nasalises the long uu and then falls away: huuṁ-gaa.
items.gloss_en: the first person presumptive, which is not होगा

learn.explanation_en: The presumptive does keep person in the first and second, which sets it apart from the past auxiliary. मैं हूँगा, not मैं होगा — and you can hear where it comes from, because हूँ is the present form for मैं and हूँगा is that same form carried forward. Used on its own like this, with no other verb in the sentence, it covers both readings at once: मैं घर पर हूँगा is I will be at home and also I am probably at home, and context decides which. That double life is not an accident, and the next level explains it.

examples.note: घर is oblique before पर, and the verb stands alone with no participle.
Said by a woman — the gender still shows even in the first person.
The third person, and here the guessing reading is the natural one.

common_error.why_en: होगा belongs to the third person. मैं has its own form, built from the हूँ you have used since Module 5.

practice.question: होना · मैं · masculine · presumptive
practice.explanation_en: The first person form is हूँगा, built from हूँ rather than from हो.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: मैं गया हूँगा — the perfective participle with the first person presumptive auxiliary.

items.pronunciation_notes: होगे has no nasal at all, which is the only thing separating it from होंगे: ho-ge.
items.gloss_en: तुम has its own presumptive form

learn.title_en: होगे and होंगे differ by one hum
learn.explanation_en: तुम takes होगे and आप takes होंगे, and the two are separated by a single nasal that is easy to miss and easy to drop. This is the first time in the module that तुम and आप have not shared a form — they took the same participle and the same auxiliary in every other cell — so it is worth marking. The full set is मैं हूँगा, तू होगा, वह होगा, तुम होगे, and होंगे for आप, हम and वे. Five forms, and only two of them are new to you.

examples.note: The casual form, with no nasal.
The polite form, and the nasal is the whole difference.
Said to a woman — तुम takes the plain feminine होगी.

common_error.why_en: होंगे belongs to आप, हम and वे. तुम has held plural agreement everywhere else in this module, so this is the one place it breaks step.

practice.question: होना · तुम · masculine · presumptive
practice.explanation_en: तुम takes होगे — the same shape as होंगे but without the nasal.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: तुम कहाँ जाते होगे — the habitual participle with the presumptive auxiliary.

summary.recap_en: The presumptive is done. It keeps gender and number like the past auxiliary but also keeps person in the first and second — मैं हूँगा and तुम होगे — which is the only place तुम and आप part company in this module. Used alone it means both will be and probably is, and the next level explains why.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the real future, which turns out to be the same set of endings you have just learnt.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ऊँ is long and nasal, and the ending falls away after it: jaa-uuṁ-gaa.
items.gloss_en: the future is one word, and it marks person

learn.title_en: The only tense with no auxiliary
learn.explanation_en: Every form in this module so far has been a participle plus होना. The future is not. It is one word — stem plus a personal ending — and it is the only tense in Hindi built that way. That has a consequence worth naming: because there is no auxiliary to carry the person, the verb itself has to, so the future is also the only tense where the ending changes for who is speaking as well as for gender. मैं जाऊँगा is I will go, and the -ऊँगा belongs to मैं alone.

examples.note: One word, and the ending is specific to मैं.
The destination takes no postposition, as always with जाना.
कल means both yesterday and tomorrow — the tense tells you which.

common_error.why_en: There is no auxiliary in the future. Adding one is the natural reflex after twenty levels of participle plus होना, and it is wrong.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · मैं · masculine · simple future
practice.explanation_en: The first person future ending is -ऊँगा, and nothing follows it.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: मैं जाता हूँगा — I probably go. The first option is the future, which is a different thing.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two vowels meet in the middle with no glide: jaa-e-gaa, three light beats.

learn.explanation_en: वह जाएगा is he will go. The ending -एगा covers तू and वह alike, which is the one place those two pronouns share a form. Look at the shape of it: an -ए, then -गा. Every future ending in Hindi ends in that same -गा, -गे or -गी, and what varies in front of it is a vowel chosen by person. Once you see the -गा as fixed, there are only four vowel patterns to learn rather than eight whole endings.

examples.note: The -एगा ending, shared with तू.

examples.english: the boy will go to school
examples.note: A noun subject in the direct form, since nothing follows it.
आना takes the same ending: आ plus एगा.

common_error.why_en: -ऊँगा belongs to मैं. In the future the ending identifies the person, so the wrong ending names the wrong person.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · वह · masculine · simple future

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: वह गया होगा — he has probably gone. The first is the future, which makes no claim about the past at all.

items.pronunciation_notes: The nasal sits before the ग and is a hum rather than a full n: jaa-eṁ-ge.

learn.explanation_en: The plural ending is -एंगे, and it covers आप, हम and वे together, exactly as हैं and थे did. So तुम and आप are back to differing here, just as they did in the presumptive: तुम जाओगे against आप जाएंगे. Those two forms are worth drilling as a pair, because getting them mixed makes a polite sentence sound casual halfway through, which is more noticeable to a listener than a plain grammatical slip.

examples.note: The plural ending, shared with आप and हम.
हम takes the same ending as वे.
The polite question, and one you will be asked constantly.

common_error.why_en: -एगा is singular. With no auxiliary present, the ending is the only thing marking the plural.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · वे · masculine plural · simple future
practice.question_read_as: jaanaa · ve · masculine plural · simple future
practice.explanation_en: -एंगे is the plural ending, used by आप, हम and वे alike.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: वे जा रहे होंगे — they are probably going right now.

summary.recap_en: The future is one word with no auxiliary, which makes it the only tense where the verb itself carries person. Every ending finishes in -गा, -गे or -गी, and what changes in front of that is a vowel chosen by person: -ऊँ for मैं, -ए for वह, -ओ for तुम, -एं for the plural.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the feminine endings, and the form तुम keeps for itself.

items.pronunciation_notes: Identical to the masculine until the last syllable, which lifts to a long ii: jaa-uuṁ-gii.

learn.title_en: Swap the last vowel and nothing else
learn.explanation_en: मैं जाऊँगी is the same word with -गा changed to -गी. The person marking sits in the middle of the word, in the -ऊँ, and the gender sits at the end, in the -गा or -गी. Two pieces of information in one word, in fixed positions. That is worth noticing because it makes the future easy to correct on the fly: if you have named the wrong person, fix the middle; if you have named the wrong gender, fix the last letter.

examples.note: Said by a woman. The -ऊँ still marks मैं.
आना with the same two pieces.
A group of women — the plural middle, the feminine ending.

common_error.why_en: Getting the gender right does not fix the person. -एगी belongs to वह, and the middle of the word is what identifies मैं.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · मैं · feminine · simple future
practice.explanation_en: -ऊँ for मैं in the middle, -गी for feminine at the end.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective present cell?
game.explanation_en: मैं गई हूँ — the perfective participle with a present auxiliary.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three light syllables ending on a long ii: jaa-e-gii.

learn.explanation_en: As in every other tense, वह covers both genders and the verb carries the difference. वह जाएगा and वह जाएगी are one letter apart and mean he will go and she will go. Since the future is a single word, that letter is the only thing in the whole sentence pointing at who you mean, which makes it more load-bearing here than anywhere else in the module — there is no auxiliary standing behind it to reinforce the choice.

examples.note: One letter from the masculine, and a different person entirely.

examples.english: the girl will go to school
examples.note: A feminine noun subject, and the ending reads it.
बहन is Class 5 feminine, which the verb has to know.

common_error.why_en: Not ungrammatical, but it means he. With no auxiliary present, this single letter is doing all the work.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · वह (feminine) · simple future
practice.explanation_en: -ए for the third person, -गी for feminine.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह जा रही है — she is going right now.

items.pronunciation_notes: The middle vowel is a plain o with no nasal at all: jaa-o-ge.
items.gloss_en: the ending तुम keeps for itself

learn.explanation_en: तुम has its own future ending, -ओगे, which nothing else uses. That is the second time तुम has broken away from आप — it also did so in the presumptive, with होगे against होंगे — and both breaks are in the same corner of the grammar. Everywhere else in this module the two behaved identically. The pair to drill is तुम जाओगे and आप जाएंगे, because these are the forms you will use to ask someone what they are going to do, and the register has to hold across the whole sentence.

examples.note: The -ओगे ending, used by तुम alone.
The casual version of the question from the last level.
Said to a woman — the ending turns feminine as everywhere else.

common_error.why_en: -एंगे belongs to आप, हम and वे. Using it with तुम mixes two registers inside one sentence.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · तुम · masculine · simple future
practice.explanation_en: तुम takes -ओगे, which no other pronoun uses.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: तुम जाते हो — you go, as a habit.

summary.recap_en: Person sits in the middle of the future ending and gender sits at the end, so the two can be corrected independently. तुम keeps -ओगे for itself, which with होगे is the second and last place it parts company from आप.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the future with other verbs, and why होगा looked like a future all along.

levels.title_en: The future, and where होगा came from

items.pronunciation_notes: The stem कर shortens against the ending, coming out as ka-ruuṁ-gaa.

learn.explanation_en: करना gives the stem कर, and the first person future ending attaches straight onto it: करूँगा. Notice that the ending swallows the stem's own vowel — कर plus ऊँगा does not give करऊँगा but करूँगा, with the two running together. That happens with every consonant-final stem and it is not an irregularity, just what the spelling does when two vowels meet. मैं करूँगा is I will do, and it is one of the most useful single words in the language.

examples.note: The stem and the ending have merged into one vowel.
Possibly the most-used sentence in any language.
The plural of the same verb, with the same merging.

common_error.why_en: The stem vowel and the ending vowel merge into one long ऊँ. Writing both out separately is a spelling error rather than a grammatical one, but it is a visible one.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: करना · मैं · masculine · simple future
practice.explanation_en: Stem कर plus the first person masculine ending, merged into करूँगा.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: मैं कर रहा हूँ — I am doing it right now.

items.pronunciation_notes: The aspirated kh carries a real puff and the vowels stay separate: khaa-e-gaa.
items.gloss_en: a transitive verb in the future, with no ने

learn.title_en: The future is safe for every verb
learn.explanation_en: खाना is transitive, and in the future that changes nothing: वह खाना खाएगा, with a plain subject and the ending agreeing with it. This is the third time the point has come up and it is the last. The construction that treats transitive verbs differently belongs to the perfective and to nothing else, so the habitual, the continuous and the future are all safe ground. Only when you want to say he ate rather than he eats, is eating or will eat does the question arise, and that is Module 9.

examples.note: A plain subject, and the ending agrees with it.
खाना is the noun for food, standing in front of the verb as its object.
पढ़ना is transitive too, and the ending still reads the subject.

common_error.why_en: खाता is the habitual participle of the verb. The object here is the noun खाना, which happens to look identical to the infinitive.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: खाना · वह · masculine · simple future
practice.explanation_en: Third person masculine singular takes -एगा, whatever the verb's transitivity.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual past cell?
game.explanation_en: वह खाता था — he used to eat.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two syllables, open o then a falling gaa — identical to the presumptive auxiliary because it is one.
items.gloss_en: होगा is the future of होना, which explains everything

learn.title_en: The presumptive was a future all along
learn.explanation_en: Apply the future endings to होना and you get हूँगा, होगा, होगे, होंगे — which is exactly the presumptive set from levels twenty and twenty-one. They are not similar; they are the same forms. होना's future means will be, and when it sits behind another participle that becomes a guess, because saying he will be gone in Hindi is how you say he must be gone. That is why होगा looked like a future: it is one. Level twenty told you it was not the future, and what that really meant was that it is not the future of the main verb — वह जाएगा and वह गया होगा say completely different things, and now you can see why both contain a -गा.

examples.english: he will be, he is probably
examples.note: One form, two readings, decided by whether anything stands in front of it.
With कल naming a future time, only the future reading survives.
With a participle in front, it becomes a guess about the past instead.

common_error.why_en: The future needs no auxiliary at all, and होगा is itself a future. Stacking them says nothing extra.

practice.question: होना · वह · masculine · simple future
practice.explanation_en: होना is slightly irregular here — the future is होगा rather than the होएगा the rule would predict.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: वह गया होगा — the perfective participle with होगा behind it.

summary.recap_en: Every verb takes the same future endings, and transitive verbs are as safe here as anywhere outside the perfective. The presumptive auxiliary turns out to be the future of होना, which is why होगा looked like a future — the difference is whether the -गा is on the main verb or on a होना standing behind it.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the future in conversation, and how to say you will not.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three nasal hums in a row across the three words, which is unusual and worth hearing.

learn.title_en: नहीं in front, for the last time
learn.explanation_en: The placement has not changed once in this module and it does not change now: नहीं goes before the verb. Since the future is a single word, this is the simplest case of all — two words, in that order. मैं नहीं जाऊँगा is I will not go, and it is a complete refusal with nothing else needed. Hindi also has a separate negative for the future, न, but नहीं is what you will hear in ordinary speech and it is the safe default.

examples.note: Two words after the pronoun, and nothing else required.
The same shape with feminine agreement.
And again in the plural.

common_error.why_en: नहीं comes before the verb, not after it. Putting it at the end sounds like an afterthought rather than a refusal.

practice.question: मैं जाऊँगा · negative
practice.explanation_en: नहीं goes between the subject and the verb, as it has throughout the module.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: मैं नहीं जाता — I do not go, with the auxiliary dropped as usually happens after नहीं.

items.pronunciation_notes: करेंगे has the nasal on the middle syllable: ka-reṁ-ge.

learn.explanation_en: आप क्या करेंगे is the polite way to ask someone their plans, and तुम क्या करोगे is the casual one. Both are worth having ready, because this is the question that opens most conversations about anything upcoming. Note that आप takes the plural ending here, exactly as it has taken plural agreement everywhere else — the only pronoun that ever surprised you on this point was तुम, twice, and this is not one of those times.

examples.note: The polite form, and the safe default.
The casual form, with तुम's own ending.
A different question word in the same slot.

common_error.why_en: -ओगे belongs to तुम. Opening politely with आप and finishing casually is more noticeable than a plain grammatical slip.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: करना · आप · simple future
practice.explanation_en: आप takes the plural ending -एंगे, as it takes plural agreement everywhere.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: आप क्या कर रहे हैं — what are you doing right now.

items.pronunciation_notes: The middle vowel of रहना disappears under the ending: ra-he-gii, three light beats.
items.gloss_en: plans, and the gender that has to be chosen

learn.explanation_en: Every line of this exchange has a future in it and no two endings are alike: करोगे for तुम, जाऊँगा for a male speaker talking about himself, जाएगी for a third person who is female, and रहेगी for the same person. Four sentences and the ending has told you the person and the gender each time, without a single auxiliary. That is the future's whole character — one word doing the work that two words do everywhere else in this module.

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: No, she will stay at home.

common_error.why_en: बहन is feminine, and वह will not tell your listener that. The ending is the only place the gender appears.

practice.question: क्या बहन भी ___?
practice.explanation_en: One sister, feminine and third person, so -एगी.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: The speaker says रहेगी — third person, singular, feminine, agreeing with बहन.

summary.recap_en: नहीं goes in front of the future exactly as it has in front of every other tense. आप takes the plural ending and तुम keeps -ओगे, and mixing the two breaks the register mid-sentence. With no auxiliary anywhere, the ending alone carries both person and gender.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the imperatives — तू कर, तुम करो, आप कीजिए — where the register system decides the whole form.
